provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Edu family batch. Membership category: monthly add-ons held under one family's tuition. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Every belt rank in order, the techniques and forms each one tests, typical months between belt tests, testing fees, and what happens if a student isn't ready yet
pageStructurePlus.why: Parents commit to years of tuition when they can see the road to black belt. A visible rank path answers 'how long does this take' before they ask.

pageStructurePlus.section: Character and anti-bullying for karate kids
pageStructurePlus.contains: What the dojo teaches about focus, respect and handling a bully without fighting, how instructors reward it on the mat, and how parents hear about progress
pageStructurePlus.why: Most parents aren't buying karate for the kicks. They are buying confidence for a shy child or calm for an anxious one, and they decide on that.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Which elementary schools the dojo van collects from, pickup times by school, homework time, the class that follows, and late pickup rules
pageStructurePlus.why: Working parents choose an after-school martial arts programme the way they choose childcare: by route, hours and who is driving.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Adult jiu jitsu gi and no-gi classes, open mat, kickboxing and fundamentals, beginner etiquette, what to wear, and drop-in rules for visiting grapplers
pageStructurePlus.why: Adults decide whether they'll fit in before they walk on the mat. A plain beginner path and an open mat schedule get them through the door.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Party length, games and board breaking, group size, what the dojo provides, the deposit and the waiver every guest's parent signs
pageStructurePlus.why: A party puts a dozen families inside the dojo at once. Parents book it when the price and waiver process are clear online.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Who qualifies for the competition team, extra sparring classes, the tournament calendar, travel costs and the gear each fighter needs
pageStructurePlus.why: Committed families look for a school with a path past the basic class. A team page keeps the strongest students from leaving for a bigger academy.

designDirections.name: Trial Class Poster
designDirections.bestFor: Single-location karate and taekwondo schools that need trial bookings more than anything else
designDirections.headlineSample: Kids' karate in {City}. Your first class is free.
designDirections.whyItFits: Ultramarine and the geometric display read like a tournament banner, and the split hero keeps the trial class button beside the action shot.

designDirections.name: Little Black Belts
designDirections.bestFor: Family martial arts schools with kids' programmes by age, a belt path and an after-school pickup
designDirections.headlineSample: Confidence, focus and martial arts for {City} kids
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo. Sky Kite's soft rounded type feels safe to a parent, and the card stack sorts classes by age the way parents search.

designDirections.name: Mat Room
designDirections.bestFor: Adult jiu jitsu and kickboxing academies with a respected head instructor and a competition team
designDirections.headlineSample: Brazilian jiu jitsu and kickboxing in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: A dark basalt ground with lime accents looks like a lit mat at night, and it signals an academy for serious adults rather than a kids' class.

openers.line: Your Google listing for the dojo has class hours and a phone number but no website, so a parent searching karate classes for kids in {City} can't see a schedule or the trial offer.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what a parent would find behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing goes to the dojo's Facebook page, where the newest kids' class schedule is a post from months back. Parents want belt classes by age they can read on a phone.
openers.hook: Tap the link and find the most recent schedule post. Note its date.
openers.linkLine: Your martial arts schedule by age, on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: The martial arts school site on your listing still shows an old free-host banner and a summer camp from a past year. A parent comparing dojos notices that first.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one stale detail: an old camp, old class times, a dead form. Note it.

openers.line: I opened your karate school site on my phone and the class timetable ran off the side of the screen. Parents look up martial arts classes from a phone in the school pickup line.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same martial arts school, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: The only way to book a trial class at the dojo is to call, and the phone rings while you're teaching on the mat. A trial class button would take those bookings during class.
openers.hook: Look for a trial or free class form anywhere on their listing or page. If it's call-only, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A trial class booking that works while you teach: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your belt promotion posts are the best thing on the dojo's page, and they scroll away in a week. A belt rank path that shows what each colour takes would keep that pride working.
openers.hook: Find their latest belt test or promotion post and note which ranks were promoted.
openers.linkLine: Your belt path, from white to black: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your Google reviews are full of parents talking about a child's confidence after karate. Those reviews should sit next to the trial class button, not three taps away.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase a parent wrote about their child. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Parent reviews next to the kids' martial arts classes: {demo-link}

openers.line: Late summer is when parents line up after-school activities, and martial arts schools with a visible kids' schedule get the trial bookings first.
openers.hook: Use this from late July to mid-September, or in December for January starts. Name the season.
openers.linkLine: A back-to-school karate page, ready to book: {demo-link}

openers.line: Parents look up taekwondo and karate classes after the kids are in bed. At that hour your dojo's only option is a phone nobody answers.
openers.hook: Look for comments or reviews asking 'how do I sign up' or 'what ages'. Note one.
openers.linkLine: A dojo page that takes a trial booking at 10pm: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're looking for an assistant instructor for the kids' martial arts classes. Good black belts check what the school looks like online before they reply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring or 'join our team' note. Note the date and the role.
openers.linkLine: A martial arts school page with a join-the-team section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts mention picking kids up from nearby elementary schools for after-school karate. Parents in {Neighborhood} want to see which schools are on the route before they call.
openers.hook: Only if their bio or posts mention pickup or an after-school programme. Note the schools named.
openers.linkLine: An after-school martial arts page with the pickup route: {demo-link}

openers.line: I couldn't find a monthly price for kids' martial arts anywhere on your pages. A parent comparing three dojos tends to skip the one that says call for pricing.
openers.hook: Check the listing, posts and any site for tuition. If none is shown, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A martial arts tuition page with a clear starting price: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your head instructor's black belt rank and lineage are why serious families choose a martial arts school, and they're not anywhere a new parent would look.
openers.hook: Look for rank, lineage or association membership in their bio or posts. Never invent a credential.
openers.linkLine: Your instructors' ranks next to the classes they teach: {demo-link}

openers.line: It sounds like most new students at the dojo are siblings and classmates of current ones. Those parents still look the martial arts school up before the first class.
openers.hook: Look for reviews saying 'my friend recommended' or posts welcoming a sibling. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a referred karate parent would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted was a big day for the dojo. A belt test or tournament result like that should be the first thing a new martial arts parent sees.
openers.hook: Pick their newest belt test, tournament or seminar post and name it exactly.
openers.linkLine: That martial arts moment, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted looked like a proud day at the dojo.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and only found the listing and your social pages, with no kids' class schedule or trial class button. I put together a sample martial arts school page with classes by age, a belt path and a trial booking, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my message got buried under class sign-ups. Here's the sample site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has kids' classes by age, a belt rank path, a trial class booking with a waiver and an after-school section. If it's not for you, say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for martial arts schools here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss between classes. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with kids' classes by age, a belt path and a trial class booking, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link to look at after the last class?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and schedule changes. For a dojo your size I'd normally quote about {Build Price}."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes before your first class one afternoon this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears, and it's live before the next belt test."

objections.objection: We don't put prices online. Parents come in for an intro first.
objections.handler: "Keep the intro. The page shows a starting monthly price and books the intro lesson, so the parent who walks in has already decided the dojo is in budget."

objections.objection: Our member software came with a website.
objections.handler: "It handles billing well. The bundled page can't explain your belt path or after-school route. The site sits in front of it and sends sign-ups straight into the same system."

objections.objection: All our students come from word of mouth.
objections.handler: "That says the classes are good. The referred parent still looks the dojo up that night, and right now they find a phone number. The site is where a classmate's recommendation lands."

objections.objection: One of my black belts does our website.
objections.handler: "Great, keep them involved. Happy to hand over what I built, the belt path and the trial booking. If it isn't live before back-to-school, the offer stands."

objections.objection: Summer is slow, I'm not spending now.
objections.handler: "Summer is exactly when to build. Parents start looking at after-school karate in August, and the page needs to be ranking before they do."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's classes by age, a belt path and a trial booking. A couple of new students cover it in their first year."

email.subject: Martial arts site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for martial arts schools in {City}, and I put together a sample one for {Business Name} with a trial class booking. I'll email you the link so you can look after class. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} dojo demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — January is when a lot of families make a fresh start on kids' activities, and martial arts trial classes pick up with it. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to what a couple of new students pay in their first year of tuition, never to an hourly rate.
Price kids' programmes by age group, not by page. Each age band has its own schedule, belt path and trial booking.
The trial class booking with a signed waiver is its own line. It is the page's whole job.
Only quote the after-school pickup page for schools that run a van. Otherwise leave it out of scope.
Keep monthly add-ons under one family's monthly tuition. Anything higher gets cut when a student quits.
Sell back-to-school work in June and July and January work in November, never during the rush.

lineItems.description: Max when the age group has its own timetable, belt path, trial booking and gallery with parent photo consent noted.
Max when every rank lists its techniques, forms, testing fee and typical time to the next belt, with a printable chart.

lineItems.item: Trial class booking with digital waiver
lineItems.description: Max with age-based routing to the right class, a signed waiver, uniform size question and reminder texts.
Max when it lists every school on the van route with pickup times and a waitlist per school.
Max with date availability, a deposit, guest count and a waiver link sent to every guest's parent.
Max with weekly camp sessions, sibling pricing, lunch options and a medical and pickup form.
Max when the trial booking, waiver, belt path and pricing are all translated, not only the home page.

whatElseYouSell.name: Belt test photo and video day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One belt test shot properly, with written parent consent for every child shown, fills the dojo's gallery and a month of posts."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, booked on the next belt test date. Consent forms go home the week before.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for the dojo
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "New class times, belt promotions and trial offers on the dojo's Google profile every week, so a parent searching karate nearby sees an active school."

whatElseYouSell.name: Parent review requests after belt promotions
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The day after a child earns a new belt, the parent gets a short text asking for a review while they're still proud."

whatElseYouSell.name: Back-to-school and January martial arts ad campaigns
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Local ads for kids' karate timed to back-to-school and January, pointed at the trial class page, switched off once classes fill."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in June for August, and in November for January. Ad spend is on top.

whatElseYouSell.name: School flyer and PTA newsletter artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A flyer for the elementary school folder and a PTA newsletter ad, both with the dojo's trial class code, so the backpack sends parents to the page."
whatElseYouSell.when: Before back-to-school, once the trial class page is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Dojo window and lobby signage for the trial offer
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Window graphics and a lobby sign with a scan code to book a trial class, so parents waiting for a sibling at the dojo can sign up on the spot."

whatElseYouSell.name: Summer martial arts camp campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A spring push for summer camp weeks at the dojo, on the site and in parent groups, before families lock in other camps."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in February, run March through May.

whatElseYouSell.name: Monthly dojo post planning
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "You teach, I plan the month of martial arts posts around belt tests, tournaments and open trial classes."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, if they say posting is the part they never get to.

withoutAI.route: The martial arts supply shop that outfits the dojo
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your uniform and sparring gear supplier sells to every karate school in the region and has no order page for schools. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Supply shops live on school accounts. Their customer list is a list of dojos, and the head instructor's word is the introduction.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The tournament your team fights at runs registration through a paper form and a group chat. I'll build the registration and divisions page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Promoters need entries and every school owner knows them. A competition team coach is a trusted voice.

withoutAI.route: Other after-school activities on the same pickup route
withoutAI.whoPays: Each tutoring centre or art class, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The tutoring centre and art class your karate parents also use need the same after-school page. I build them on the dojo's template."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: They share families and pickup times with the dojo, and they often cross-refer. One parent sees all three sites.

withoutAI.route: The plaza landlord where the dojo rents
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The plaza your martial arts school sits in has empty units and no leasing page. You can introduce me to the property manager."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Landlords pay to fill units, and a long-term tenant who pays on time is an introduction they take seriously.

withoutAI.route: The physical therapist who treats your adult grapplers
withoutAI.whoPays: The clinic, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The clinic your jiu jitsu students see for shoulders and knees needs a page aimed at combat athletes. I'll build it with the dojo as a referral partner."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Injured grapplers trust the clinic their coach names, so the clinic gains from the link as much as the dojo does.

withoutAI.whoPays: The wrestling club, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The youth wrestling club down the road shares half your BJJ kids in the off-season. I'll build their registration page on the same layout."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Wrestling and jiu jitsu families overlap, and the coaches already send kids to each other.

withAI.route: Uniform size assistant for the supply shop
withAI.pitchLine: "Parents enter a child's height and weight, and the assistant picks the right uniform and sparring gear size from the supply shop's chart."
withAI.whyItWorks: Wrong sizes are the shop's biggest return cost, and every dojo it serves sends parents the same question.

withAI.route: Division and bracket question assistant for tournaments
withAI.pitchLine: "Parents ask which division their child fights in by age, belt and weight, and the assistant answers from the tournament rules before the promoter wakes up."
withAI.whyItWorks: Promoters drown in the same questions the week before an event. One event pays for it.

withAI.route: Enrolment question assistant for neighbouring after-school programmes
withAI.pitchLine: "The same parent assistant you built for the dojo, loaded with the tutoring centre's schedule, pickup times and prices."
withAI.whyItWorks: It's configuration of something you already run, sold through a neighbour who shares the families.

withAI.route: Leasing enquiry assistant for the plaza landlord
withAI.pitchLine: "Tenants asking about an empty unit next to the martial arts school get size, rent and parking answers at any hour, and the landlord gets a showing request."
withAI.whyItWorks: Empty units cost the landlord every month. A tour request is easy to value.

withAI.route: Appointment request assistant for the physical therapy clinic
withAI.pitchLine: "An injured jiu jitsu student describes where it hurts and when it started, and the clinic gets a tidy appointment request instead of a voicemail."
withAI.whyItWorks: Clinics lose patients to slow callbacks. It never diagnoses; it only collects the request and books.

withAI.route: Practice and meet schedule assistant for the wrestling club
withAI.pitchLine: "Wrestling parents text 'is practice on tonight' and get the answer from the club's own calendar, with weigh-in times for meets."
withAI.whyItWorks: Volunteer-run clubs answer the same question all season. A small monthly fee beats a coach's evening.

softwareAI.name: Trial class follow-up texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A family that came to one trial class gets a friendly text that evening and an enrolment offer two days later, so the karate trial doesn't just fade."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their trial offer, the enrolment price and access to the booking calendar.

softwareAI.name: Digital waiver and front-desk check-in
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every trial student's parent signs the dojo waiver on a phone before class, and the instructor sees who's arriving and their age on a tablet."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: At build, or the first time a trial family shows up unsigned. Needs their current waiver wording, checked by their insurer.

softwareAI.name: Belt test eligibility tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Classes attended since the last belt, techniques signed off and who's ready to test, without counting attendance cards the night before."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, before the next belt test. Needs their rank requirements and class attendance, even if it's on paper cards.

softwareAI.name: Parent DM responder for class times and tuition
softwareAI.pitchLine: "'What age can my son start karate' and 'what's the price' get an answer in seconds from the dojo's own schedule, with a trial class link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the schedule by age, tuition and trial rules, updated whenever they change. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Missed-class nudges for students
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A student who misses a week of martial arts classes gets a 'we miss you on the mat' text to the parent, before missing turns into quitting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs attendance data from check-in and the parent phone list.

softwareAI.name: Tuition autopay and failed-card follow-up
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Monthly dojo tuition charged automatically, and a polite text goes out when a card fails, so you never chase a parent in the lobby."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, if they still bill by hand or cash. Needs their payment account and the family list.

softwareAI.name: Dojo phone receptionist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "While you're teaching on the mat, the dojo phone still gets answered, the class question gets handled and the trial class gets booked."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once they trust you. Needs the schedule, tuition, trial rules and booking access. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Home practice video library by belt
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Students log in and see the forms and techniques for their own belt, so practice at home matches what the instructor teaches."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs short videos of each rank's forms, recorded by the instructor, and the belt list.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for the dojo
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every parent review gets a warm reply drafted in the head instructor's voice, naming the child's class but never their full name."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside the review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Caption writer for belt test and tournament posts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Post the belt promotion or tournament result, and a caption in the dojo's voice with the ranks named is ready to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs a few past captions to learn the voice and the rule on naming children. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Birthday party booking and deposit
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Parents pick an open Saturday slot for a martial arts party, pay the deposit and get a waiver link to send every guest."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, if they host parties. Needs party times, price, guest limits and the waiver.

softwareAI.name: Pause-instead-of-cancel flow
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a parent asks to cancel karate, they're offered a pause or a different class time first. Plenty of kids come back after soccer season."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their cancellation rules and a pause policy they're willing to offer.

softwareAI.name: Student progress notes for parents
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The instructor speaks a few words after class about a student, and the parent gets a short, kind progress note on their child's martial arts."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the instructor's sign-off on every note and the parent contact list. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Curriculum answer bot for assistant instructors
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Assistant instructors check the dojo's own curriculum and class plans for any belt, instead of interrupting the head instructor mid-class."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, for schools with assistant instructors. Needs the written curriculum and approval of every answer. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: After-school pickup roster and van checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Which kids ride the dojo van from which school today, checked off at pickup and drop-off, with absences texted in by parents."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, only for schools with an after-school van. Needs the school list, pickup times and the roster.

softwareAI.name: Pro shop gear ordering
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Parents order the next uniform, sparring gear or belt online, and the dojo sees one order list before the supplier deadline."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their gear list, sizes and prices.

softwareAI.name: Lapsed student win-back
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Families who left the martial arts school last season get a note before back-to-school with a return-class offer. Some just drifted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the list of past students and when they stopped.

softwareAI.name: Class fit quiz for parents
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A parent answers a few questions about age, temperament and goals, and the quiz suggests the right martial arts class and books the trial."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the programme list and the instructor's rules for placing kids. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Quit-risk flags from attendance
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each Monday the head instructor sees which martial arts students are drifting, based on attendance and missed belt tests, with a suggested call."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after several months of check-in data. Needs attendance and belt history. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Tournament team travel and fee tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Which competitors are entered in which tournament, who has paid the entry fee and who needs a hotel, in one list for the team coach."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, only for schools with a competition team. Needs the tournament calendar and team list.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the belt tracker and trial follow-up for every independent dojo
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Martial arts schools, monthly per school
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built belt test tracking and trial follow-up for one karate school. Every independent dojo counts attendance cards the same way."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first school taught you the workflow and paid for it. Dojo owners talk at every tournament and seminar.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The national or regional style federation
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member school a trial-class site template with your rank structure built in, as a federation benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Federations need renewals and a reason to stay affiliated. One deal reaches many school owners who already trust the federation.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: School locator for a martial arts gear wholesaler
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your dojo customers want students. A school finder on your site that sends parents to the karate schools you supply keeps those accounts loyal."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Wholesalers compete for school accounts. A tool that fills their customers' classes beats a discount.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each location needs its own class schedule, trial booking and after-school route on one shared martial arts template. I build it once and roll it out."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes many locations, and franchisors already budget for local pages.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label dojo site template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency picks up karate and BJJ clients and builds from scratch. License my enrolment template with the belt path and waiver built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell them the martial arts part you've already perfected.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every tournament on your circuit needs divisions, registration and results. One platform for the whole season, built by someone who coaches a team through it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Circuits run many events a year on the same rules, so the build pays back across the season.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Certified instructor locator for a martial arts system
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Students search for a school certified in your system. A locator tied to your instructor records sends them to an affiliated dojo, not an imitation."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Headquarters care about lineage and quality. Proof that affiliation brings students makes renewals easy.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Park district martial arts class listings
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your rec centre runs karate and self-defence classes through outside instructors. A class listing and registration page for each one fills them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Rec departments contract with dojo owners already, so the client is a warm introduction to the buyer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Gymnastics and cheer gyms in the same parent circles
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Each gym, at your normal rate
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Gymnastics and cheer gyms sell to the same parents as kids' karate, with the same trial-and-enrol problem. I take the dojo template to them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The enrolment pattern carries over almost unchanged, and the martial arts site is proof they can see.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Kids' activity guide for a local parenting magazine
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your back-to-school activity guide is a print list. An online version with class times and trial links for every karate, dance and swim programme sells more listings."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Publishers sell listings to the same schools you build for, and every listing is a lead for you.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: The same dojo stack in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New martial arts schools in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I keep one karate school per side of town in {City}. The dojos in the next metro are wide open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the template, the pitch and the finished martial arts proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rescue stalled dojo member software setups
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Someone half-set-up your member billing and trial booking and disappeared. I can finish it on a setup I've already run for another dojo."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stuck school owners have already decided to buy. They need someone who has done it before.

upsellLadder.offer: Dojo site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The martial arts site and the care plan go on one contract, so a new class time is a text to me, not a night at the computer."

upsellLadder.trigger: A trial family arrives without a signed waiver, or they mention the paper waiver pile.
upsellLadder.line: "That unsigned trial waiver is exactly what a phone waiver before class stops."

upsellLadder.offer: Trial class follow-up texts and parent review requests
upsellLadder.trigger: A month of trial bookings shows families who came to one karate class and never enrolled.
upsellLadder.line: "Those trial families liked the class. Let's text them that evening and ask the happy parents for reviews."

upsellLadder.offer: Belt test photo and video day
upsellLadder.trigger: They post the date of the next belt test.
upsellLadder.line: "Your next belt test is the best photo day of the season. Let's shoot it with consent forms sent home first."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention counting attendance cards to decide who's ready for the belt test.
upsellLadder.line: "No more counting attendance cards. The tracker shows who's ready for the next belt."

upsellLadder.offer: Parent DM responder for class times and tuition
upsellLadder.trigger: They say evenings go on answering 'what age' and 'how much' messages about kids' karate.
upsellLadder.line: "Those after-bedtime karate questions get answered from your schedule while you sleep."

upsellLadder.offer: Back-to-school and January martial arts ad campaigns
upsellLadder.trigger: Kids' classes show open spots six weeks before school starts or before New Year.
upsellLadder.line: "The kids' karate classes have room. Let's run local ads to the trial page before the sign-up rush."

upsellLadder.offer: Introduction to the martial arts supply shop
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention the supply shop owner asking who built the dojo site.
upsellLadder.line: "Your gear supplier serves every dojo around here and has no order page. Would you introduce me?"
